When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **100**, STRONG BUY vs Regime state **60** with risk off bias, macro regime CONTRACTION at **70%**
Contrarian measures how washed out sentiment is. The regime measures where the economy is heading. Trust the regime for how much risk to carry and the contrarian score for when a bounce can start, so scale in with small pieces.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **5**/**10**, 5+ signals aligned vs Divergence composite zone CALM, with **16** of **43** pairs diverging
The Crash Index counts stress signals and the composite says correlations between assets are not breaking in a coordinated way. Trust the Crash Index for the risk level. The calm composite tells you the damage is orderly so far.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **5**/**10**, action zone vs VIX Spike tier **1** of **4**, backwardation inactive
Price signals shout alarm while the options market has not priced a panic. Trust the Crash Index on direction of risk. The low VIX tier tells you the fear has not arrived yet, which leaves room for it to rise.
Today's tension
Five crash signals are lit while the contrarian gauge sits at **100** and the VIX tier stays low at **1** of **4**.
Bull
Contrarian score **100** flags capitulation, and the selling is already deep: the S&P 500 is **-3.9%** over five days and the Russell 2000 is **-4.6%**. Washed out markets bounce hard once forced sellers finish.
Bear
The macro regime reads CONTRACTION at **70%** confidence, and **4** risk off signals line up behind a regime score of **60**. Asia, Europe, the US and crypto are all falling together, so no region offers shelter.
The tell: Watch the VIX Spike tier and the term structure. A climb above tier **1** with backwardation switching on says the selling is turning into panic. A flat tier **1** with backwardation still off says this is an orderly pullback.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together are starting to move apart. Correlation drift is the size of that shift.

Here 16 of 43 pairs are diverging, which lands in the CALM zone, yet the mother jaws score reads 100. The biggest breaks all score 80.

The 10 year minus 2 year yield spread moved from -0.59 to +0.32. Copper against gold moved from +0.86 to -0.13.

NVDA against AMD moved from -0.91 to +0.23. Gold miners against gold moved from -0.27 to +0.50, and VIX against realized volatility moved from -0.53 to +0.06.

Old relationships are loosening across rates, metals, chips and volatility. Expect surprises in pair trades and hedges that worked last month.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Every region is down, so there is no clean leader. Asia is weakest at the lagging end, with the KOSPI at -5.2% over five days against the Shanghai Composite at -2.2%.

Europe holds up best, with the Swiss index at -0.4% and the Euro Stoxx 50 at -1.8%. The US sits in between at -3.9% for the S&P 500 and -4.6% for the Russell 2000.

Crypto is the sharpest, with SOL at -6.3% and ETH at -8.3%. Crypto trades around the clock and tends to show risk appetite first, so its weakness points to a soft open for US small caps and high beta stocks.

Relative strength in Europe says the selling has not turned into a global rush yet.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 5/10 · ALARM — 5+ signals aligned, action zone
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The two gauges disagree in a way that makes sense. The Crash Index at 5 of 10 says price and breadth signals are stressed.

The VIX Spike Detector sits at tier 1 of 4 (BROAD) with a 50% probability, and backwardation is off, meaning near term options are not costing more than later ones. Put them together and you get a market that is falling in an orderly way.

Sellers are active, yet nobody is paying up for emergency protection. The skew trigger is on, so some investors are already buying downside puts.

That is the first sign fear is building. If the tier rises and backwardation switches on, price stress and options stress will agree, and that is when you cut risk faster.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 5/10 — several signals are aligned, a real stress probability is building.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
